title: Micro-chunk ACK window and idempotent resume token for SSE streams
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: We continue to see customer outages and developer confusion when long-lived SSE streams disconnect mid-function-call or mid-structured-output. Existing resume tokens are opaque and coarse-grained which forces clients to re-request large windows of output; function-call boundaries are frequently re-executed during reconnects, causing duplication or state mismatch for webhook-like tool integrations.

Goal: Implement a micro-chunk acknowledgement (ACK) window plus an idempotent, versioned resume token (v2) for the SSE endpoint to: (1) minimize replays after reconnect, (2) preserve structured output / function-call boundaries across interruptions, (3) enable server-side bounded retention that supports graceful reconnection under backpressure, and (4) remain backwards-compatible with v1 clients.

Design summary:
- Micro-chunking: break tokenized output into logical micro-chunks (typical size ~256-1024 bytes of serialized payload) annotated with incremental sequence numbers and chunk checksums. Each micro-chunk is emitted as a single SSE data event with a chunk header prefix: "chunk-id:<seq>|chk:<crc32>|type:<payload|meta|fn-call>".
- ACK window: client may supply last_ack_seq on reconnect or send periodic ack events on the open stream. Server maintains a sliding retention window (configurable per-tenant, default 30s / 10k chunks) and will serve missing micro-chunks up to the retention boundary.
- Idempotent resume token v2: token encodes model-version, stream-id, last-emitted-seq, retention-hash, and a short HMAC (rotating key). Token is base64-url encoded and intentionally small. On reconnect, token is validated and used to find the stream cursor; if out-of-window, server responds with a short structured error recommending client fallback to full-response or non-stream path.
- Function-call and structured outputs: chunk metadata marks edges of structured objects and function-call payloads. The server ensures that a function-call boundary (fn-call:end) is only acknowledged when the server has flushed the entire call payload and any tool call result has been confirmed. If a reconnect occurs mid-fn-call, client can request replay from the preceding chunk boundary and the client-side SDK will deduplicate function invocations using the function-call-id embedded in chunk metadata.
- Backpressure and flow control: introduce per-connection credit window (default 5 outstanding micro-chunks). Clients can request increased credit with an in-stream control event. Server will honor but may throttle by tenant policy.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Pros: minimizes duplicate work on tool integrations, reduces bandwidth and latency on reconnects, provides clear semantics around structured outputs, and enables safer canary rollouts because resume is deterministic.
- Cons: increased server-side state (retention window) and slightly more complex chunk encoding/SDK changes. HMAC key rotation requires backward compatibility handling when validating old tokens.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Resume token v2 format documented and implemented with tests.
2) Micro-chunk events emitted with correct headers and chunk CRC validated on server and (optionally) on client.
3) Reconnect flow replays minimal delta when within retention; returns structured guidance when out of window.
4) Function-call deduplication works across reconnects in end-to-end tests with a mock tool that logs invocations.
5) Backpressure credit controls prevent unbounded memory growth in server and are configurable per-tenant.
6) Backwards compatibility: v1 clients receive prior behavior; v2 clients get micro-chunk benefits.

Implementation notes:
- Server: extend stream formatter to emit micro-chunks. Add lightweight retention index keyed by stream-id -> sequence ranges (in-memory with eviction; persisted in Redis for cross-process lookup).
- Token service: new encoder/decoder with short HMAC using rotation table keyed by epoch id. Token size target < 128 bytes.
- SDK changes: JS/Go SDKs must (a) parse chunk headers and rehydrate structured events, (b) expose an ack() API and automatic ack batching, (c) provide opt-in credit window tuning and automatic retry with resume token.
- Telemetry: new metrics: sse.reconnects.by_reason, sse.replayed_bytes_per_reconnect, sse.out_of_window_reconnects, sse.fncall-duplicate-rate. Add tracing span for resume token validation.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge server-side feature behind feature flag per-tenant. Ship JS SDK opt-in parsing to users for early testing.
2) Canary for low-volume tenants with extended retention (60s) for two weeks, monitor duplicate function-call rate and sse.out_of_window_reconnects.
3) Expand to 20% tenants and enable automatic ack batching.
4) Full rollout and retire v1 resume token after 6 weeks of stable telemetry, with notice to customers.

Migration guidance for customers:
- Opt-in: set header X-Redwood-SSE-Resume: v2 and use SDKs with ack/resume helpers.
- Compatibility: if you cannot upgrade, you will keep prior semantics; recommend SDK upgrade for tool-heavy workloads.

Related artifacts and references: design doc and sequence diagrams in Confluence, unit/integ tests in repo, plus an incident that motivated this work (INC-2025-14).
